description: Implement the Android-free CORE of the POC: a deterministic interlude state machine and a safe-resume guard, with all Android dependencies behind injectable interfaces, plus the full set of required pure-JVM JUnit4 tests. This is the heart of the capability spike's correctness and is testable off-device. No Android framework classes may be referenced by the core logic classes (only plain Java), so the tests run under testOptions.unitTests.returnDefaultValues without needing a device. This feature depends on FEAT-001 (module exists).
steps: In mediaexperiment/src/main/java/com/scenevibe/tvcompanionpoc/mediaexperiment/core/ create an Android-free enum InterludeState modeling the sequence: IDLE, SCANNING, FOCUS_REQUESTED, FOCUS_GRANTED, FOCUS_DENIED, PAUSE_SENT, PAUSE_CONFIRMED, PAUSE_TIMEOUT, OVERLAY_ATTACHED, VIDEO_PLAYING, VIDEO_COMPLETED, VIDEO_ERROR, PLAY_SENT, PLAY_CONFIRMED, PLAY_TIMEOUT, STOPPED/CLEANED. Keep names explicit and bounded.

Create InterludeStateMachine (plain Java) that enforces legal transitions ONLY. It must: never move to a PLAY_SENT state unless the guard permits (see SafeResumeGuard); treat an out-of-order or unexpected event as a transition to a cleanup/STOPPED state rather than crashing; expose the current state and a bounded transition log (enum values only, no content strings).

Create a SessionTarget value object (plain Java): fields packageName, mediaId (nullable), title (nullable), subtitle (nullable), durationMs. Create a PlaybackSnapshot-equivalent plain-Java value object (packageName, state code as int mirroring PlaybackState constants but defined as POC-local int constants to stay Android-free, mediaId, title, subtitle, durationMs). Add POC-local playback state int constants (NONE/PLAYING/PAUSED/etc.) so the core does not import android.media.session.PlaybackState.

Create SafeResumeGuard (plain Java, Android-free) implementing the user's exact rule: PLAY may be issued ONLY if ALL hold — this POC successfully sent the PAUSE; PAUSED was subsequently observed; the target session/package is still the same; the media identity has not clearly changed; the user has not switched to another media app; and the interlude ended normally OR the POC is explicitly performing emergency cleanup. Expose a pure boolean decision method taking the recorded pause-ownership facts + the latest observed snapshot + the original target. Port the fail-closed media-identity comparison idea from MediaIdentityMatcher (title/duration/mediaId) into a small Android-free helper in this module (do NOT import the production class).

Create bounded timeout handling as pure logic: the state machine takes an injected clock (e.g. a LongSupplier or a Clock seam) and a configurable pause-confirmation timeout and play-confirmation timeout (ms). A confirmation that does not arrive before the deadline transitions to PAUSE_TIMEOUT / PLAY_TIMEOUT and reports UNSUPPORTED/NOT CONFIRMED. 'Command sent' MUST NOT be treated as success — only an observed PAUSED/PLAYING snapshot confirms.

Define Android-facing seams as interfaces in the core package so the Android layer (FEAT-003) implements them: AudioFocusPort (requestTransientMayDuck() -> GRANTED/DENIED, abandon()), MediaControlPort (pause(), play() — fire-and-forget transport dispatch), OverlayVideoPort (attach(), playLocalVideo(), remove()), LocalAudioPort (playShortClip(), stop()). The state machine orchestrates these through the ports; the ports are trivially mockable in tests.

Create a bounded Diagnostics value holder (plain Java) capturing ONLY: selected package, playback state name, available PlaybackState action flags (as a bounded set of booleans/int), mediaId presence (boolean), audio focus request result, pause command sent (boolean), pause confirmed/timeout, overlay attached (boolean), local video started/completed/error, play command sent (boolean), resume confirmed/timeout. No content text, no credentials, no titles beyond what identity matching needs internally (never logged).

Write pure-JVM JUnit4 tests in mediaexperiment/src/test/java/com/scenevibe/tvcompanionpoc/mediaexperiment/ following the DisplayCountdownTest style. Required cases (the user enumerated these): (a) state machine happy path PLAYING->focus->pause->confirmed->overlay->video->completed->same-target->play->confirmed; (b) focus DENIED => DO NOT play local audio, no pause, clean abandon; (c) pause timeout => report UNSUPPORTED/NOT CONFIRMED and DO NOT continue to the interlude; (d) session replacement (different package appears) => guard fails, no PLAY, overlay removed, focus released; (e) media identity change (same package, different mediaId/title) => guard fails, no PLAY; (f) overlay/video failure (OverlayVideoPort errors) => emergency cleanup, no PLAY unless pause was confirmed-and-owned, overlay removed, focus abandoned; (g) repeated STOP cleanup is idempotent (calling stop/emergency twice leaves a clean STOPPED state, ports abandoned once-effectively, no exception); (h) NO accidental PLAY after an unsupported/unconfirmed pause (guard returns false, play() port never invoked).

Assert the ports in tests via recording fakes (e.g. a RecordingMediaControlPort that counts pause()/play() calls) so the tests prove the real decision core would call or NOT call transport controls. Each test must fail if the guard/state-machine logic were reverted (e.g. assert play() invoked exactly 0 times in the denied/timeout/identity-change cases, exactly 1 time only in the fully-confirmed-owned case).
Run `:mediaexperiment:testDebugUnitTest` and confirm all new tests pass. Do NOT add any claim in code comments or tests that this proves real ducking or real Prime pause — these are logic tests only.
Commit (e.g. 'feat(poc): add Android-free interlude state machine, safe-resume guard, and JVM tests'). Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: Core classes (InterludeState, InterludeStateMachine, SafeResumeGuard, value objects, ports, Diagnostics) contain NO import of android.* — they are pure Java and compile/run under JUnit without a device.
SafeResumeGuard returns true ONLY when all six user-specified conditions hold; it returns false for focus-denied, pause-timeout, session-replacement, media-identity-change, and app-switch inputs.

`:mediaexperiment:testDebugUnitTest` passes with tests covering all nine required scenarios (happy path, focus denied, pause timeout, session replacement, media identity change, overlay/video failure, repeated STOP cleanup idempotency, no-accidental-PLAY-after-unsupported-pause).
In the focus-denied, pause-timeout, session-replacement, media-identity-change, and overlay-failure tests, the recording MediaControlPort records ZERO play() calls.
'Command sent' is distinct from 'confirmed' in both the state machine and the tests (a sent-but-unconfirmed pause does not advance to the interlude).
verification: Run `:mediaexperiment:testDebugUnitTest --console=plain` and confirm BUILD SUCCESSFUL with the new test classes executed and 0 failures.
Open the generated test report (mediaexperiment/build/reports/tests/testDebugUnitTest/index.html) or the test XML and confirm all nine required scenario tests ran.
Run `grep -rL 'import android' mediaexperiment/src/main/java/.../core/` conceptually — confirm the core package files have no android imports.
